verdict.root_cause: At 08:13:17Z an automated pipeline (platform-automation) updated shippingservice's image reference to a tag that names a different service, and the prior image value is recorded as absent — a mistagged/mistargeted rollout rather than a version bump (tr_4eed29ed8cd8). The consequence is visible in shippingservice's own log stream: normal Rust/tonic quote-serving lines stop after 08:06:06, and from 08:13:38 onward the stream contains only JVM/OpenTelemetry Java agent startup banners repeating every ~60-65s with no request-handling lines — a wrong-runtime container in a restart loop, and an emitter change consistent with a different service's image running under the shippingservice label (tr_af45c73ad1a3). Downstream, every failing checkout trace fails on the same deepest span, checkoutservice's outbound GetQuote to ShippingService, with no shippingservice server span beneath it and ~2-3ms durations, i.e. RPCs rejected at connect time rather than a slow dependency (tr_de43511de1d1), producing the partial (~0.28 peak) error ratio on checkoutservice (tr_e1b79455abe4) as requests land between restart attempts. No change of any kind was recorded on checkoutservice itself (tr_aac7acaa0876), so checkout is a victim, not the origin.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge on shippingservice as origin and on a mistagged image as mechanism. (1) Timing and trigger: the only recorded change anywhere in the dispatched set is the shippingservice image update ~2.5 minutes before the incident marker, by automation, with a tag naming a different service (tr_4eed29ed8cd8). (2) Effect at the service: shippingservice stops emitting serving lines and emits only repeated JVM startup banners, and those banners are a different runtime family than the earlier tonic/Rust serving lines — the log emitter changed at the same time the image changed, which is what running the wrong image looks like (tr_af45c73ad1a3). (3) Effect on the alerting service: traces put the deepest error on checkoutservice's client span to ShippingService/GetQuote with no server span underneath and no latency elongation, exactly the signature of connecting to a process that is not up, and they affirmatively clear cart, product catalog, currency, frontend, and checkout's own logic (tr_de43511de1d1). Checkoutservice's own change stream is empty across onset, ruling out self-inflicted change there (tr_aac7acaa0876). The metrics dispatch on shippingservice returned nothing for numerator or denominator (tr_6a7ac5b47690); the specialist correctly declined to read that as health, and it is at least consistent with a process not staying up long enough to be scraped, though a selector/schema mismatch is the competing explanation and this evidence cannot separate them. The corpus contains a near-identical prior case (cart-bad-image-tag) where a downstream service showed no error metrics and was wrongly cleared — that pattern is a caution here, not proof, and I am relying on the change record plus the runtime mismatch in logs, not on the empty metric. Remediation follows the mechanism: revert the image reference to the correct shippingservice tag; a restart alone would only re-launch the wrong image.
open_questions: The empty shippingservice metric series (tr_6a7ac5b47690) was never resolved — it could be a crash-looping process that never gets scraped, or a wrong metric/label schema in the query. Until that is settled there is no quantified error or traffic baseline for shippingservice itself, and no independent metric confirmation of the outage.

quoteservice alerted at 08:19:15 and was never dispatched on. The shipping logs contain no reference to quoteservice or any upstream (tr_af45c73ad1a3), so whether quoteservice is a second victim, a co-casualty of the same pipeline run, or an independent problem is unknown.

accountingservice, emailservice, and frauddetectionservice alerted at 08:19:30 and were not investigated. Their relationship to the checkout failure path (likely async order-completion consumers) is inferred, not shown; triage flagged 5 unmeasured edges crossed.

The exact identity of the wrongly-tagged image was not confirmed — the change record notes the tag names a different service (tr_4eed29ed8cd8) but which service's image is actually running under the shippingservice label was not verified.

The prior image value is recorded as absent, so the correct rollback target is not established by this evidence; the last-known-good shippingservice image reference needs to be recovered before reverting.

Whether the same automation run mistagged other services was not checked. Only checkoutservice and shippingservice change streams were queried, and the checkoutservice query covered only a 15-minute window rather than the intended 60-minute lookback.

Why checkoutservice's error ratio peaks near 0.28 rather than approaching total failure is not directly demonstrated. The restart-loop-window explanation is plausible but was not confirmed against a per-minute correlation of restart timing and error timing.
